name: Azulejo
summary: Painted tin-glazed tiles that cover the walls of churches, palaces and streets in Portugal and Spain. A painter works in blue or in many colours on a white glaze, and one scene runs across many tiles.

philosophy.core_thesis: A wall becomes a picture when many square tiles are painted as one scene on a white tin glaze.
design_principles: Paint the scene on the raw tin glaze, so that each stroke dries at once and cannot be changed.
Plan the scene across a grid of square tiles, about 13 to 15 cm each, and number the tiles on the back.
Use cobalt blue alone for narrative panels; use many colours for pattern carpets.
Repeat a pattern tile in a 2 by 2 or 4 by 4 group to make a carpet of stars and flowers.
Frame a large panel with painted volutes, shells, putti and a cornice.
Cover the wall to the ceiling, or to a dado of about 1.5 m, with no bare patch.
Keep the tile body thin and the glaze thick, about 0.5 mm.
Use a bold blue and yellow in the early pattern tiles and a soft blue in the 18th-century panels.
anti_patterns: A printed pattern with no brush line
A bare grey grout line between tiles
A photograph printed on the tile
A scene that stops at the edge of one tile

form.shape: Square tiles in panels for church naves, cloisters, palace walls, stairs, kitchens and street fronts; frieze tiles and corner tiles.
form.profile: A flat face with a soft swell of the thick glaze; the tile edge is slightly rounded and not cut square.
form.foot_and_rim: The back is rough and unglazed with ribs for the mortar; the edge of a panel runs into painted frames or a stone moulding.
form.proportion: A tile is about 13 to 15 cm square and 8 to 12 mm thick; a panel has 100 or more tiles.
rules: Paint across the joints, not tile by tile.
Keep the blue to one or two tones, from a pale wash to a deep line.
Close each panel with a painted frame or a border.

bodies.rule: Use a buff or red earthenware that fires soft and takes a thick tin glaze. Keep dense bodies out: the glaze must stay thick and soft.

methods: pressing the tile in a wooden mould
drying the tile in the shade
pricking a paper cartoon and pouncing the pattern
numbering the tiles on the back
forming.joins: Tiles are set in lime mortar, with joints of 1 to 2 mm, and the panel is set from the top down.
forming.details: Pounce dots in the painted line, a soft blur of the blue at the edge, small chips at the corners and the mark of the pottery on the back.

glaze.pattern: Blue narrative scenes in baroque frames, carpet patterns of stars and flowers in blue, yellow and green, and later floral and geometric tiles.
glaze.gloss: Glossy and thick, about 60 to 85 GU.
glaze.wear: The glaze chips at the corners and shows the buff body; the blue stays strong and the white turns a little grey.

palette.strategy: Cobalt blue on a white tin glaze; early and folk work adds manganese purple, copper green and antimony yellow.

firing.kiln: A wood-fired kiln; the tiles stand on edge in stacks, with stilts between them.
processes: a biscuit firing of the pressed tile
a second firing for the glaze
firing.scale: Lisbon workshops made whole church walls in a year; a panel used hundreds of tiles and two or three painters.
firing.signs: Three stilt marks on the face or edge, numbers on the back, and a soft blue blur where the cobalt sank into the glaze.

pieces.form: Blue narrative panel of a saint in a painted frame with volutes and putti
Pattern tile of 14 cm in blue, yellow and green, to repeat in a 2 by 2 group
Frieze tile with a blue scroll and shell border
Early Seville tile with raised lines of cuerda seca in green and brown

positive: hand-painted cobalt blue on white tin glaze
baroque frame with shells and putti
carpet pattern of stars and flowers

canonical_works.work: The Visitation, altar tile of the Reales Alcázares, Seville
Tile panels of the Church of São Vicente de Fora, Lisbon
Great Panorama of Lisbon, tile panel

evidence.title: Azulejo panels in the Madre de Deus cloister

emotion.target_response: A warm, civic pride: the viewer reads the story on the wall and feels the age and the sun of a southern town.

use_cases: a church, cloister or street facade clad in painted tile
a kitchen or stair wall in painted tile
a museum label on Iberian tile painting
avoid_when: the brief needs a modern minimal tile
the brief is for large format porcelain

modifiers.how: Keep the tin glaze, use a smaller single motif in each tile, and add a corner motif.
Change to a white quartz body, a clear glaze and painted tulips and carnations with a raised red.
